Armor Pieces

Parts, skins and cloth for armor — because someone else at spawn is wearing your diamond set.

Minecraft 26.2 · Fabric · Client & Server · version 0.3.0 · what 0.3.0 brought →

Themed sets, every socket filled — the mod's knightly, court and wayfarer, and the pack sets beside them
Every armor skin on one diamond suit — the plate itself changed, not something hung on it
Sixty sets with nothing about them chosen — armor, skin, cloth, part, material and every fitting rolled
One circlet, seven gems — the fitting takes a second material
The advanced smithing table, holding the whole court suit beside it — the chestplate's sockets and their fittings as rows of icons, its own trim, skin and cloth under them, and Remove, the one way any of it comes off again

Your library

The gallery is everything published. Your library is your selection out of it - and it starts here, in this browser, with no account: the packs and pieces you save are kept on this machine and can be exported to a file. Signing in offers to keep exactly these in a library instead, which is what makes them follow you to another machine - and what lets you publish a pack, host one, or share a set. About this site

Armor Pieces is a Minecraft mod, and this is the site around it: a wiki, a gallery of pieces and packs, the editor in your browser, and a library for the packs people make.

Who runs it

The site and the mod are made and run by mattjes. The responsible party for everything published here, and the address to write to about any of it, is contact@armorpieces.example. Bug reports and feature requests are better on the issue tracker, where other people can find them too.

What it is not

NOT AN OFFICIAL MINECRAFT PRODUCT. NOT APPROVED BY OR ASSOCIATED WITH MOJANG OR MICROSOFT.

Armor Pieces is a fan-made mod. It is not made by, endorsed by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft. Minecraft is a trademark of Mojang Synergies AB. The site follows the Minecraft Usage Guidelines: it does not serve the game or any of its files, it does not sell anything, it carries no advertising, and nothing about an account here changes anything in the game.

Where the money is

Nowhere, on purpose. The mod is downloaded from Modrinth and CurseForge, whose creator programmes pay authors per download under their own terms. That is the only income the project has, and the site costs it nothing. There are no paid tiers, no affiliate links and no ads. If a way to support the project directly is ever added, it will buy nothing that only the supporter can use.

The site follows the Minecraft Usage Guidelines: it does not serve the game or any of its files, it does not sell anything, it carries no advertising, and nothing about an account here changes anything in the game.

Where the money is

Nowhere, on purpose. The mod is downloaded from Modrinth and CurseForge, whose creator programmes pay authors per download under their own terms. How the mod works, how pieces are found and applied, and how to make your own.

Armor Pieces gives one piece of armor four layers of decoration, each an independent choice:

a piece hung on one of twelve sockets: a crest on the helmet, spaulders on the shoulders, a sash on the belt, spurs on the heels;
a skin that changes what the plate itself is made of;
a cloth worn over the chest, carrying the design of any banner;
and vanilla’s own trim underneath them all.

Every one of them is applied at a smithing table, and none replaces another. A helmet can carry a skin, a trim, a crest, a browband and a pair of horns at once.

Account
Sign in

An account is a sign-in through a provider. The site never sees a password, stores only the provider's id and a display name, and nothing about it changes anything in the game.

No sign-in provider is configured on this deployment yet. The operator sets the providers' client ids in the environment.

Signing in you agree to the terms; what is stored is on the privacy page. You must be old enough for the provider's own terms.

What an account is for
Your library: the packs and pieces you keep, and the sets you save. Packs you author live there too - uploaded as zips or saved from the editor, with versions, private by default. Unlisted has a link; public goes to review and then to the gallery with a thumbnail per piece.
The desktop editor: sign the Blockbench plugin in with an eight-character code, and Your library appears in its pack manager.
Nothing else. No badge, no tier, no effect in the game, ever.

You do not need one to look, to keep what you like, or to dress a figure: the gallery, a shelf of your own, the wardrobe and the whole editor work in this browser without an account, and signing in offers to keep exactly what is there. What an account adds is what a browser cannot do on its own: publishing a pack, hosting one, a link to a set, and the same shelf on another machine.

Publish

A pack goes to the gallery as a list of published pieces. Offering it files one review per piece of yours that is not published yet, plus one for the pack itself – so a piece is reviewed once ever, a piece already in the gallery goes in as a link, and the pack becomes public when the last of its pieces has been approved.

Offer this pack to the gallery…

Armor Pieces in Blockbench

The authoring plugin for Armor Pieces, running in your browser. Pick a piece to open it on the player figure in armor: the same rig, sheets, material preview and datapack editor the desktop plugin gives you, driven by the repository's own Python under Pyodide.

The figure wears the studio set - the mod's own plate skin, in iron, on the game's exact boxes - because the game's textures are Mojang's and this page does not serve them. Use my game... points the editor at your own copy (the launcher's jar, or any resource pack); it is read into this browser and nowhere else, and from then on the figure wears real armor.
Signed in. These are the pieces in your library on the site - 0 of them
